Claude said: 
> Every surface uses ToLocalTime(); RestaurantOptions.ResolveTimeZone() has no caller and the container sets no TZ, so a deployed instance shows guests UTC. I kept the existing convention here rather than putting two time formats on one screen — the static header and the island are one page. The fix needs a decision §13 never made (12- vs 24-hour), so it wants its own slice before M5.

The UTC convention is impractical. 
While internally, it makes sense to store events in UTC, 
we know a restaurant has a physical location 
which has an IANA time zone 
Looks like §13 has 
| `RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE` | `America/New_York` | rendering only |
which we should use to render any date and time in the application. 
For example, lets say the restaurant is in Asia/Tokyo and a customer is away in America/New York 
the customer logs into the website to see past orders. what time zone should we display? 
my decision is the user's local time zone is irrelevant. We should always display and render all date time
in restaurant time zone 
which now adds a new requirement. 
the website footer should show the current date time accurate to the second and ticking continuously 
on every single page on the website 
in restaurant time zone
when we refresh the page, 
this clock should update from the server 
but for normal operation, I think once we have the datetime from the server we can trust the local computer clock to keep it up to date. 
you may use performance dot now or similar technology to keep the clock in sync 
always keep in mind that not just the look and style should be mindful of responsive mobile design 
but also the performance should be mindful that most users will be on a phone or similar handheld device 
so the web browser or operating system could do things to save battery 
please fix and also there is an error in the razor 
and remember to update documentation when changing code
